question: Does multi-scale agreement between total-field magnetic and isostatic-gravity boundaries recover spatially withheld mapped faults better than the published H42 basin-margin/scarp baseline?
hypothesis: Buried faults or contacts can juxtapose rocks with both magnetic-susceptibility and density contrasts. Co-located, sharp gradient vectors that remain directionally concordant across scales may identify blind or uncatalogued structures without using the training catalogue to shape the score.

not_used: labels.tif while constructing the score surface
previous submission rasters in score construction

frozen_operator.gaussian_mask_handling: normalized convolution over valid cells; nearest boundary mode
frozen_operator.gradient: numpy.gradient on the smoothed fields in the common raster grid
frozen_operator.magnitude_normalization: independent 99th percentile over valid footprint cells, clipped to [0,1]
frozen_operator.multiscale_aggregation: pixelwise median of the three single-scale responses; requires concordance at at least two of three scales
frozen_operator.emission: stable score-descending greedy packing; 4.0-pixel minimum separation; 40,000 binary pixels; exclude evaluation-domain cells within 2 pixels of training traces

holdout.protocol_source: buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE41 scripts/holdout_h42.py; copied owner report saved as evidence/h42_holdout_owner_reference.json
holdout.truth: withheld positives from the published catalogue; not the hidden competition truth
holdout.metric: official 300-m triangular-kernel DTI formula, applied to the spatial holdout without the official known-catalogue mask so held-out positives remain truth

reference.provenance: GEMSDOE41 owner-maintained report; not organizer-confirmed and not yet independently reproduced at registration time

outcome.interpretation: candidate failed the frozen local spatial-catalogue gate; do not submit or offer it as a submission
